title: Cornell's Embarrassing T-Shirt Study Cures the Fear of Publishing
alt_title_1: The Spotlight Effect: Why Half as Many People Notice Your Mistakes
alt_title_2: Thomas Gilovich's 2000 Experiment on Public Self-Consciousness
description_hook: In 2000, Cornell University psychologists Thomas Gilovich, Victoria Medvec, and Kenneth Savitsky proved the Spotlight Effect using an embarrassing Barry Manilow T-shirt. Here is why overestimating scrutiny holds back builders and creators.

scenes.headline: The Imaginary Audience Blocking Your Work
scenes.stat_label: HOW MUCH WE OVERESTIMATE PUBLIC SCRUTINY
bullets: Great drafts die in private folders out of social fear
We assume peers dissect every awkward early attempt
scenes.narration: How many gifted builders never publish an essay, launch a tool, or negotiate a raise because they fear looking awkward in public?
scenes.source: Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (2000)

scenes.headline: Gilovich's 2000 Cornell T-Shirt Experiment
scenes.stat_label: PREDICTED VS ACTUAL CLASSMATES WHO NOTICED
bullets: Students walked into class wearing a giant Barry Manilow shirt
Wearers guessed ~50% noticed; only ~23% could recall it
scenes.narration: In 2000, Cornell psychologists Thomas Gilovich, Victoria Medvec, and Kenneth Savitsky sent students into a classroom wearing an embarrassing Barry Manilow shirt. Wearers guessed half the room noticed; barely twenty-three percent actually did.
scenes.source: Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky, 'The Spotlight Effect in Social Judgment', JPSP (2000)

scenes.headline: Mistaking Your Inner Stage for Everyone's Feed
scenes.left_body: Assumes every peer critiques your draft -> years of paralysis
scenes.right_body: Early reps go unnoticed -> free practice until craft gets sharp
scenes.narration: They called this egocentric illusion the Spotlight Effect. Because you stand at the center of your own stage, you double-count how closely busy strangers track your missteps.

scenes.headline: Use Early Obscurity as Free Practice Armor
scenes.stat_subtext: 25 low-pressure public reps -> real mastery before crowds arrive
scenes.narration: Turn obscurity into your training shield: publish messy early reps freely while nobody is watching, compounding real skill long before a crowd arrives.

scenes.headline: Everyone Is Busy Staring at Their Own Mirror
scenes.stat_label: NOBODY IS GRADING YOUR ROUGH EARLY REPS
bullets: Clumsy version one is forgotten by everyone except you
Version twenty-five builds the career you actually want
scenes.narration: Everyone else is busy worrying about their own shirt, so hit publish on your work today.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb inspired by Gilovich et al. (2000)
